engineNotes.v1: Measured on the v1 engine: three opponent archetypes, win rate weighted 0.40 of the composite score.
engineNotes.v2.1: Measured on the v2.1 engine: nine opponent archetypes, win rate weighted 0.30 with 0.10 given to a fun/participation signal, plus three combat-modeling fixes (toughness-as-damage creatures, planeswalker commanders, dual-color lands). v2.1 scores are systematically lower because the opponent field is harder -- that is not the deck getting worse.
engineNotes.v2.2: Measured on the v2.2 engine: the same nine-archetype opponent field as v2.1, extended with modelled +1/+1 counters (growth, doubling, proliferate) and combat keywords (flying, menace, trample, deathtouch, first strike, lifelink) -- see docs/mechanics-design-v2.2.md. Win rate is weighted 0.35 and fun 0.05, both reweighted from v2.1's 0.30/0.10 (the Fun rung alone keeps fun at 0.10). v2.2 scores are not comparable to v1 or v2.1 -- different weights, and modelling more of what a deck's own cards do changes the numbers independent of any change in the deck itself.

engineBoundaryNote: Tuned/Tuned-2/Enhance-2/Max-2 were measured on the v1 engine; Fun and Alt builds ran on v2.1, a harder opponent field with different scoring weights. Never compare a Score or Win% across that boundary -- only within one engine generation. The 44 alt-commander evaluations added for the rest of the lineup (every variant outside the six original flagships) ran on v2.2, a third generation again not comparable to the other two.

1o.honestRead: Holds up. Teneb is a genuine reanimator, which is what this shell already wants, and it measures a hair above Betor (+0.2 — inside noise). Betor's end-step lifegain-to-counters engine is invisible to the model, so the true gap likely favours Betor. Swap only if you prefer the play pattern, not for the number.

3e.honestRead: Real gain, real cost. Hazel measures +4.5 over Gitrog, but the optimizer's response to her is to strip TEN lands from a 48-land lands-matter deck — she pays off tokens, not landfall. That is not a minor tweak; it converts the Golgari Land Engine into a different deck. Adopt only if you want that rebuild.

5o.honestRead: Treat the +13.2 as unreliable. Iroas only beats Quintorius in the model because the engine cannot see devotion and so treats it as a permanent 7/4 body. Forced to behave as the enchantment it usually is, Iroas scores 59.6 — identical to Quintorius. This deck's 50 nonland permanents average 1.22 red/white pips, so a typical board reaches roughly 5.5 devotion against the 7 Iroas needs. It will usually not be a creature.

1a.honestRead: Modest gap, essentially within noise. Slimefoot's sacrifice-and-drain loop and Lathril's go-wide Elf engine both lean on effects (death triggers, token-swarm mana sinks) the model only partially credits, so treat +0.1 as a coin flip rather than a real edge -- keep Slimefoot.

1b.honestRead: Felothar already ranks first of sixteen. Its toughness-as-power and anti-Defender text are real, legible value the model scores well; no alternative measured beats it.

1c.altCommander: Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose
1c.honestRead: Real gap, but Liesa's own text is more invisible to the model than Vito's. The command-zone life tax and the 'whenever a player casts a spell, lose 2 life' drain are both outside anything the engine pattern-matches, so her true score sits higher than 70.7 -- Vito's lifegain-doubling is comparatively simple and well-credited. Treat the +15.0 gap with real skepticism.

1e.honestRead: Real gap. Ghave's counters-into-Saprolings-into-counters loop converts through tokens, and tokens are modelled as extra power on the creature that makes them rather than a separate, resilient board -- that undersells Ghave's actual wipe-resilience. Rishkar's one-shot ETB counters on up to two creatures is simpler and fully visible, which is most of why it measures ahead. Treat the gap as real but somewhat overstated.

2o.honestRead: Large gap, but The Reaper's whole identity -- -1/-1 counters and stealing opponents' creatures when they die with one -- sits entirely outside the model (counters only track +1/+1 growth; there is no steal-on-death pattern). Mazirek's sacrifice-triggered +1/+1 counter engine is squarely inside the modelled counter growth, so it measures fairly. The real gap is smaller than 17.8, but Mazirek is a genuine, well-supported upgrade for a Jund sacrifice/counters shell either way.

2a.honestRead: Xanathar's stax-flavoured upkeep lock (opponent can't cast, you may play their top card) has no matching pattern in the classifier at all -- it reads as a vanilla body. Grimgrin's self-counters-and-removal loop is squarely inside the model's growth and removal patterns. Treat +10.3 as overstated; Xanathar's real disruption value is simply invisible here.

2b.honestRead: Sheoldred's graveyard-recursion-plus-symmetric-drain kit is mostly legible (reanimation, drain), and Kalitas's repeatable removal-into-a-token measures only +3.1 above it -- inside the range where either is a reasonable pick. No strong recommendation either way.

2e.honestRead: Oloro already ranks first of sixteen on its own lifegain-into-cards loop. No alternative measured beats it.

3o.honestRead: Small gap, close to noise. Obuun's land-animation combat trigger isn't a pattern the classifier recognizes at all, so its real value is understated; treat this as a wash rather than a recommendation to swap.

3c.honestRead: Aesi's extra-land-drop-into-a-card-per-landfall is simple, repeatable draw the model credits correctly, so this is a real comparison. Rishkar's ETB counters-and-mana-ability engine still measures well ahead -- a genuine, well-supported upgrade, though it trades a card-advantage plan for a counters-and-ramp one, not a free upgrade to the same deck.

3d.altCommander: Dion, Bahamut's Dominant // Bahamut, Warden of Light
3d.honestRead: Large gap, but Sythis's simple enchantment-cast lifegain-and-draw is the more transparent of the two: Dion, Bahamut's Dominant transforms into a Saga whose mass +1/+1 counters and removal chapter are exactly the kind of text this model reads well, while the model likely can't apply 'each other creature' correctly to every creature on a wide board (it has no real multi-target counter grant, only a one-shot-to-the-biggest-creature approximation) -- so even 81.1 probably understates the real Bahamut. Three of fifteen candidates also failed to resolve here (double-faced names). Treat this as a real, if imprecisely measured, gap.

3f.honestRead: Omnath's landfall payoff is a 5/5 token every land drop, and tokens are modelled as extra power on the creature that makes them rather than separate, hard-to-wipe-around bodies -- that undersells exactly what makes a wide landfall board resilient. Its death-trigger damage is also outside anything the classifier reads. Bristly Bill's counters-and-doubling engine is fully visible to the model. Treat +11.9 as a real but overstated gap.

4o.altCommander: Dion, Bahamut's Dominant // Bahamut, Warden of Light
4o.honestRead: Real gap. Kangee's flying-team pump is simple and already well-credited; Dion, Bahamut's Dominant adds a token, a keyword, and an eventual removal-and-counters transformation, all of which register cleanly. This one holds up as a plausible upgrade.

4a.honestRead: Only three candidates matched Brago's narrow identity and theme combination, so this reads on a thinner field than most other cases. Brago's blink-for-value loop (exile and return your own permanents on combat damage) has no ETB-value pattern in the classifier, while Jason Bright's sacrifice-into-a-counter-and-flying is squarely inside the modelled counter growth. Treat +10.3 as understating Brago, whose whole plan of re-triggering enter-the-battlefield effects is invisible here.

4b.honestRead: The largest gap measured, and the least trustworthy. Shorikai's real plan -- crew 8 to become a copy of a huge exiled artifact or creature -- has no equivalent in this model; its {1},{T} loot ability is the only part that registers, so 57.1 reflects almost none of the deck's actual game plan. Black Panther's damage-reflection and mana-sink counters read as simple, well-credited combat value. Do not treat 25.4 points as a real measurement of the gap between these two commanders.

4e.altCommander: Ojer Kaslem, Deepest Growth // Temple of Cultivation
4e.honestRead: Roon already ranks first of sixteen on its blink-value loop, which the model still partially undercounts (see the Brago case) -- if anything its real margin over the field is larger than shown.

5c.honestRead: Syr Gwyn's draw-on-attack is tied to 'equipped creature attacks,' a condition the classifier doesn't parse, so only partial credit for the draw shows up. Alexios's repeatable +1/+1 counter growth lands directly on himself, a creature, which is squarely inside the modelled counter growth and scores accordingly. Real gap, but adopting Alexios trades the equipment-tribal shell for a different combat plan entirely.

5d.honestRead: Aurelia's extra combat phase is one of the strongest effects in the format -- functionally two attack steps a turn -- and there is no 'additional combat' pattern in the classifier, so none of that value is scored; only her keywords (flying, vigilance, haste) register. Black Panther's counters-and-pump kit is comparatively simple and fully visible. Treat +13.9 as a significant understatement of Aurelia, not a real case for swapping.

5e.honestRead: Modest real gap. Trostani's populate-into-lifegain is simple and well-credited; Rosie Cotton's token-triggered counters engine measures a genuine but not dramatic edge. Reasonable either way.

5f.honestRead: Aryel already ranks first of sixteen on its Knight-tribal removal engine. No alternative measured beats it.

6o.honestRead: Muldrotha already ranks first of sixteen on its graveyard-replay engine, essentially tied with Titania (-0.2, inside noise). No case for swapping.

6c.honestRead: Small gap, close to noise. Nethroi's mutate-reanimation and Teshar's historic-spell reanimation are comparably legible to the model; no strong recommendation either way.

6d.honestRead: Kruphix already ranks first of sixteen. Its devotion-gated creature status is invisible to the model (devotion isn't tracked), so it's scored as an enchantment the whole game -- which, if anything, understates the risk real opponents' removal poses to it, not its value. No alternative measured beats its unlimited-hand-size and colorless-mana-saving text.

6e.honestRead: Old Stickfingers already ranks first of sixteen on its self-mill-into-reanimation-targets plan. No alternative measured beats it, and the gap to Titania is negligible.

7a.honestRead: Real gap, but Dwalin's core mechanic -- hone counters placed on Equipment, which then buff whatever creature is wearing it -- puts the counters on a noncreature permanent, which is outside the model's counter-growth scope (documented as creature-counters only, the same gap that excludes The Ozolith). Effectively none of Dwalin's namesake ability is scored; only his first strike keyword and his equipment's own stats register. Atsushi's flying, trample, and death-trigger value are all ordinary, well-credited combat text by comparison. Treat this gap as a genuine engine blind spot specific to Equipment-counter synergies, not a real power difference.

7b.honestRead: Same equipment-counters blind spot as 7a: Dwalin's hone-counter engine targets Equipment, not a creature, so it scores as just a first-strike body. Treat the gap as overstated for the same reason.

7c.honestRead: Dwalin already ranks first of sixteen for this build despite the equipment-counters blind spot working against it here too -- a sign this particular card mix is strong enough on its visible merits alone. No case for swapping.

7d.honestRead: Same equipment-counters blind spot as 7a/7b. Dwalin's namesake mechanic isn't scored; treat the gap as overstated.

7e.honestRead: Same equipment-counters blind spot as 7a/7b/7d, smaller gap here. Treat as overstated for the same reason.

8a.honestRead: Balin already ranks first of sixteen. Its Storied-gated burn is invisible to the model (Storied tracks artifact/legendary/Saga count, which isn't modelled), so if anything its real ceiling once Storied is online is higher than this score shows.

8b.honestRead: Real but modest gap. Balin's draw-on-Dwarf-ETB is credited as ordinary draw, but the Storied damage clause on top of it isn't modelled at all (see 8a) -- so 59.6 already understates Balin, and the true gap to Rose is smaller than 6.9.

8c.honestRead: Same Storied blind spot as 8b -- Balin's damage clause isn't scored, so 56.4 undersells him. Treat +8.4 as overstated.

8d.honestRead: Balin already ranks first of sixteen even with the Storied blind spot working against him (see 8a). No case for swapping.

8e.honestRead: Balin already ranks first of sixteen even with the Storied blind spot working against him (see 8a). No case for swapping.

9a.honestRead: Real gap, but Shantotto's own payoff -- growing by the exact mana value of the spell she triggers off, mid-combat -- is conditional, scaling text with no equivalent pattern in the classifier; only the 'draw a card' half of her text likely registers. Deekah's magecraft counters land on a token creature, which is fully inside the modelled counter growth and scores accordingly. Treat +11.1 as overstating the real gap.

9b.honestRead: Same Shantotto blind spot as 9a, smaller gap. Her scaling pump isn't scored; treat +5.5 as overstated.

9c.honestRead: Same Shantotto blind spot as 9a, smaller gap. Treat +4.7 as overstated.

9d.honestRead: Shantotto already ranks first of sixteen for this build despite the blind spot working against her here too (see 9a) -- a sign this card mix is strong on its visible merits alone. No case for swapping.

9e.honestRead: Same Shantotto blind spot as 9a, the largest gap among her five builds. Treat +14.0 as overstating the real difference.

10a.altCommander: Dion, Bahamut's Dominant // Bahamut, Warden of Light
10a.honestRead: Grand Arbiter's entire text is a cost reduction for you and a tax on opponents -- there is no mana-cost-modification model in this engine at all, so he scores as a vanilla body with none of his actual, format-relevant effect measured. Dion/Bahamut's flying, token-making, and eventual mass +1/+1 counters and removal are all ordinary, well-credited value. This is the clearest case in the whole batch of an engine blind spot dominating the result: the model simply cannot evaluate a tax/stax commander, and this applies to all five variants of this deck, not just this one.

10b.altCommander: Dion, Bahamut's Dominant // Bahamut, Warden of Light
10b.honestRead: Same Grand Arbiter blind spot as 10a -- his tax text isn't modelled at all. Treat this gap, and every Grand Arbiter alt-commander result in this lineup, as uninformative about his real strength.

10c.altCommander: Dion, Bahamut's Dominant // Bahamut, Warden of Light
10c.honestRead: Same Grand Arbiter blind spot as 10a. Uninformative comparison for the reason given there.

10d.honestRead: Same Grand Arbiter blind spot as 10a. Uninformative comparison for the reason given there.
